title: The Inner Temple Measurements

questions.question: After the outer and inner courts, where did the man bring Ezekiel next?
options: To the roof of the temple
To the inner sanctuary (Most Holy Place)
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:1 (ESV): "Then he brought me to the nave and measured the jambs. On each side six cubits was the breadth of the jambs—the breadth of the tent."

questions.question: What were the measurements of the nave (sanctuary)?
options: Forty cubits long and twenty cubits broad
Sixty cubits long and thirty cubits broad
A perfect cube of twenty cubits
questions.correctAnswer: Forty cubits long and twenty cubits broad
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:2 (ESV): "He measured the length of the nave, forty cubits, and its breadth, twenty cubits."

questions.question: Then the man went into the inner room. What did he call this inner room measuring twenty cubits long by twenty cubits broad?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:4 (ESV): "...The length thereof was twenty cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits, before the temple: and he said unto me, This is the most holy place." (KJV / other versions "the Most Holy Place").

questions.question: What was built against the wall of the temple all around?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:5 (ESV): "Then he measured the wall of the temple, six cubits thick, and the breadth of the side chambers, four cubits, all around the temple."

questions.question: How many stories (levels) did the side chambers have?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:6 (ESV): "And the side chambers were in three stories, one over another, thirty in each story."

questions.question: How did the side chambers increase in size from the lowest story to the highest?
options: They became wider from one story to the next
They became narrower from one story to the next
They remained exactly the same size
They became circular at the top
questions.correctAnswer: They became wider from one story to the next
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:7 (ESV): "And the side chambers broadened as they encompassed the temple from story to story; for the structure surrounding the temple went up story by story all around the temple."

questions.question: Where did the door of the lowest story side chambers lead?
options: To a terrace that was left open
Directly into the Most Holy Place
questions.correctAnswer: To a terrace that was left open
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:11 (ESV): "And the doors of the side chambers opened on the terrace that was left... "

questions.question: What decorative carvings were made on the walls of the inner temple?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:18 (ESV): "It was carved with cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Every cherub had two faces:"

questions.question: The carved cherubim had two faces. What were the two faces?
options: A human face and the face of a young lion
An eagle's face and an ox's face
A human face and a cherub face
A lion's face and a bear's face
questions.correctAnswer: A human face and the face of a young lion
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:19 (ESV): "a human face toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved on the whole temple all around."

questions.question: What material covered the posts of the nave?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:21 (ESV): "The doorposts of the nave were squared; and in front of the Holy Place was something resembling"

questions.question: There was a wooden altar, three cubits high and two cubits long. What did the man say about this wooden altar?
options: "This is the table that is before the Lord."
"This is the ark of the covenant."
questions.correctAnswer: "This is the table that is before the Lord."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:22 (ESV): "...The man said to me, 'This is the table that is before the Lord.'"

questions.question: How many doors did the nave and the Holy Place have?
options: Two doors each, with two swinging leaves apiece
One single massive door of bronze
No doors, only a heavy veil
questions.correctAnswer: Two doors each, with two swinging leaves apiece
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:23-24 (ESV): "The nave and the Holy Place had each a double door. The double doors had two leaves apiece, two swinging leaves for each door."

questions.question: What was carved on these wooden doors of the nave?
options: Cherubim and palm trees, like those carved on the walls
questions.correctAnswer: Cherubim and palm trees, like those carved on the walls
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:25 (ESV): "And on the doors of the nave were carved cherubim and palm trees, such as were carved on the walls."

questions.question: What was placed in front of the vestibule outside?
options: A bronze serpent on a pole
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:25 (ESV): "And there was a canopy of wood in front of the vestibule outside."

questions.question: In measuring the structure behind the temple at the west side, how wide was the building?
options: Seventy cubits broad and ninety cubits long
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy cubits broad and ninety cubits long
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 41:12 (ESV): "The building that was facing the separate yard on the west side was seventy cubits broad; and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length ninety cubits."

key_verse_text: "And he measured its length, twenty cubits, and its breadth, twenty cubits, in front of the nave. And he said to me, 'This is the Most Holy Place.'"
